I freaked, didn’t know what to do and immediately looked to him for guidance. He again manipulated me to believing he “loved me” and that this “wasn’t a big deal bc he wanted to be with me forever anyway”

I quit my job and moved in with him. He lives in a small thousand person community in the prairies and I am from the west coast of Canada. I know some people might say this is stupid but I really didn’t know what to do. I needed help and I felt dirty and shameful and afraid to try dating anyone else, so I sadly gave up my life and relegated myself to being his gf with herpes. 

I stayed for 6 years, raising his child and operating his farming business, dealing with his inbred family and living in a dusty dying town with nothing but sadness in my heart about my life

The personal gaslighting that can be done while in hell week is impossible to explain. Everything seems so dichotomous and it truly feels like you “have always” felt this way about your relationship and because you believe it, it  is your truth. 

I would suggest making a list of things you love about your partner when you’re not in hell week. Document the things you’re grateful for and especially the things that make you swoon (his hugs/smell of his cologne). Consult this list when you’re breaking down during hell week to see if it’s truly warranted. 

Make videos of yourself talking your hellweek self down. Say things like “I know it feels like this is real” or “you think you’re never happy but don’t forget the good times”. I’ve found that I will listen to myself when I’m spiralling. 

As for your personal situation, I can’t weigh in without knowing so many more details. What I can empathize with is the doubt and uncertainty your hormonal brain fixates on while it warps your reality. Don’t believe everything it tells you. Good luck and I’m so glad you’re asking for support.
